pr_title: Calculate the position in the stream
pr_body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.
PRs can target `3.x` if the same change was done in `master`, or is not relevant there.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.
-->

Fix #69794.
Supersedes #69808.

No need to do annoying analysis.
pr_comments:
> > No need to do annoying analysis.
> 
> There's always a need for annoying analysis. grin


This is compared to #69808.



> The only bit I'm unsure about.


It seems that it would be better to use a variable to record the position after reading the buffer.
At least `get_position` will be more reliable. As for using FileAccess reference directly in the middle, I don't have a better solution.

An alternative for now may be to simply turn off readahead for this `ResourceLoaderText::rename_dependencies()` class.

It seems to be depending on the assumption that the file pointer and the `VariantParser` are in sync, and this will not be the case with a readahead. And seeking within the file outside the `VariantParser` will also mess up the sync.

This may take some time to ensure there are no bugs in this with readahead, and might be better to do when not under time pressure.

Some other options longterm:

1) Move the readahead functionality into `FileAccess` (I mentioned this as a possibility in the original PR, but there is potential for contributors to get this wrong, by e.g. writing and reading multiple times to the same file in parallel), but maybe this is the cleanest option?
2) Totally wrap the `FileAccess` in the `VariantParser`, so it cannot be accessed from outside, and have `open()` and `close()` etc functions for the `VariantParser`.. This might create a lot of duplication of functionality.
3) Have a function to invalidate the `VariantParser` cache.
4) Detect going out of sync in `DEV_ENABLED` builds. This would at least allow catching such bugs quickly.

issue_context.title: Moving/renaming resources cause unopened/unused tscn/res files to become corrupted
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

f692b4768

### System information

Linux mint 21, forward_plus ,NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti

### Issue description

You can open the scene to view, but if you want to reproduce this issue, make sure to close the scene before moving.

The result obtained at step 2.
```node_2d.tscn before
[gd_scene load_steps=2 format=3 uid="uid://cxgwh3ypon3mj"]

[ext_resource type="Texture2D" uid="uid://xdf2u634fcd1" path="res://icon.svg" id="1_l3rl2"]

[node name="Node2D" type="Node2D"]

[node name="Icon" type="Sprite2D" parent="."]
position = Vector2(49, 62)
texture = ExtResource("1_l3rl2")
```
The result obtained at step 5.
```node_2d.tscn after
[gd_scene load_steps=2 format=3]

[ext_resource type="Texture2D" uid="uid://xdf2u634fcd1" path="res://test/icon.svg" id="1_l3rl2"]
```


### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP project in the editor;
2. Use an external editor or the `cat` command to view the text in node_2d.tscn;
3. Make sure node_2d.tscn is not open;
4. Move the icon.svg file to a different folder.
5. Repeat step 2;


### Minimal reproduction project

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10191899/MRP.zip)
comments:
Please mention when a bug is a regression, and from which version - this was made obvious by #69953 but wasn't clear from this issue.

It would be good to know which commit caused the regression so that we can assess the proposed fix properly.

This will be a regression from #69119 , sorry my bad, I didn't see it linked as it had not been bisected.

As @Rindbee correctly noticed, the code in `ResourceLoaderText::rename_dependencies` is maintaining two references to the file, and relying on the file pointer being in sync with `VariantParser::StreamFile`, which cannot be relied on any longer, the file position must be retrieved from `VariantParser::StreamFile` directly.
I just finished bisecting between beta 7 and 8 and can confirm it was caused by 5df29fec205ae10ef8678a0327112287e1950b63 #69119.
I can confirm that the regression happens in `3.x` too (#69963 will fix it).

Does this fix:
```
-[sub_resource type="Image" id="Image_och0y"]
+[sub_resource type="Image" id="Image_5rs4i"]
```

.tres file changing id every time I press f5 to run game?

I can confirm that the issue is only partially fixed.

```
A ---> B ---> C
```
For example, the C file is used in the B file, and the B is used in the A file. 
If C is renamed/moved without opening/using ~~A and~~ B, the uid of B will still be lost, which will cause a new uid to be generated when B is opened and saved again, and A will not be updated during this period.

review_comments:
Note that when EOF is reached in `VariantParser::Stream::get_char()`, `readahead_pointer` is set to 1 and `readhead_filled` is zero, in order to catch bugs etc. So this will return `UINT32_MAX`.

This should therefore be something like:

```
uint32_t _get_buffer_remaining_length() const { return eof ? 0 : readahead_filled - readahead_pointer; }
```
(unless we change the EOF values for `readahead_pointer` etc).
